children: Gujarat-based German Green Steel and Power is set to launch its initial public offering (IPO) on September 25, with the steelmaker pricing the issue at Rs 132-139 per share as it looks to raise Rs 303.9 crore at the upper end of the price band.

The issue will remain open until September 29, while the anchor bidding portion will open a day earlier on September 24. At the upper end of the band, the company is expected to have a post-issue market capitalisation of around Rs 1,047.35 crore.
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of up to Rs 290 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to Rs 13.9 crore. Investors can bid for a minimum of 107 shares and in multiples thereafter.
A significant portion of the fresh capital will be deployed towards expanding German Green Steel’s manufacturing operations at Samakhiali in Kutch and developing a hybrid wind-solar power plant.
The company also intends to use part of the proceeds to repay or prepay certain outstanding borrowings, with the balance earmarked for general corporate purposes.
Steel Manufacturing And Captive Power

German Green Steel operates an integrated iron and steel manufacturing business, with its operations concentrated in western India and a significant presence in Gujarat. Its portfolio includes thermo-mechanically treated (TMT) bars, mild steel (MS) billets and sponge iron.
The company manufactures TMT bars in sizes ranging from 8 mm to 40 mm and markets its products under the German TMT and TMX Bars brands.

It operates two manufacturing facilities in Gujarat. The Samakhiali facility is directly operated by the company, while the Viramgam plant is operated through its material subsidiary, German TMX Private Limited.
Energy costs are a significant consideration for steel manufacturers, and German Green Steel has sought to reduce its dependence on grid electricity through captive and renewable power generation.

As of December 31, 2024, captive power and renewable energy plants accounted for around 67.72 per cent of its total energy requirements. The planned hybrid wind-solar plant is expected to increase the contribution of non-grid sources to its power needs.
Profitability Improves
German Green Steel’s revenue from operations increased from Rs 892.25 crore in financial year 2022 to Rs 1,129.78 crore in FY24, representing a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 12.53 per cent.

Operating profitability grew at a faster pace. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased from Rs 39.15 crore to Rs 80.11 crore over the same period, a CAGR of 43.04 per cent.
This translated into an improvement in the EBITDA margin from 4.39 per cent in FY22 to 7.09 per cent in FY24.
Profit after tax (PAT), however, grew at a slower CAGR of 10.43 per cent, increasing from Rs 34.16 crore in FY22 to Rs 41.67 crore.
For the nine months ended December 31, 2024, the company reported revenue of Rs 979.79 crore, EBITDA of Rs 68.18 crore and PAT of Rs 32.07 crore.

The IPO has a face value of Rs 10 per share. Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) have been allocated 50 per cent of the issue, while 15 per cent has been reserved for non-institutional investors (NIIs) and 35 per cent for retail investors.
Systematix Corporate Services, Emkay Global and Pantomath Capital are the book-running lead managers, while MUFG Intime India is the registrar.
The company’s equity shares are proposed to be listed on the BSE and NSE.
